title: user-sla-tier-cost-sensitivity-heatmap-draft-feb14-2025
body:
Executive summary:

This draft collates a compact set of microbenchmarks and synthesized cost-modeled outputs to help product and SRE teams decide per-customer SLA tiers and recommended burst allowances. The focus is not absolute numbers (they vary by region/hardware) but on relative sensitivity: how much additional cost (USD per 1M tokens) a customer pays to tighten P95/P99 by common opt-in tiers.

Goals and audience:
- Audience: product pricing, SRE, solutions engineering.
- Goal: provide a lightweight artifact (heatmap + textual interpretation) to inform tier pricing, suggested autoscale buffers, and fallback rules.

Scope / what this is NOT:
- NOT a full canonical benchmark across all models/hardware. This is a targeted set across 3 representative model sizes and 2 infra classes (edge-like smaller GPU vs. core larger GPU).

Test matrix summary:
- Models: small-conversation (1.5B), medium-instruct (7B), base-chat (33B)
- Infra classes: T4-like (low-cost edge) and A100-like (core, high-throughput)
- Workloads: sessionized chat (avg 6 turns, 60 tokens/turn), bursty spikes (sustained for 30s), and steady throughput (1000 concurrent tokens/s)
- Measured: P50, P95, P99 latency (ms) and estimated addl cost per 1M tokens when enforcing a per-request latency cap via scaling/burst reserved capacity.

Methodology notes (quick):
- Synthetic client replay with realistic arrival distribution (Poisson baseline, plus periodic burst pulses).
- Cold-starts excluded (we provisioned warm pools to reproduce steady SLO tradeoffs); warmup penalty accounted separately in appendix.
- Cost model: GPU hourly effective cost amortized per token based on throughput observed under each SLO target; includes a 10% buffer for networking/overhead.

Text heatmap (rows = SLA bucket, columns = model x infra; cells = pct increase in USD per 1M tokens vs. baseline unconstrained P95):

Legend: low <5% (.), 5-15% (:), 15-30% (*), 30-60% (#), >60% (@)

Columns: [1.5B-T4] [7B-T4] [33B-T4] [1.5B-A100] [7B-A100] [33B-A100]

SLA buckets (P95 targets):
- 300ms
- 150ms
- 75ms
- 40ms

Heatmap:
300ms   : .   .   :   .   :   :
150ms   : :   :   *   :   *   *
75ms    : *   *   #   :   #   #
40ms    : #   #   @   *   @   @

Interpretation (readers: this is the core):
- At loose SLOs (300ms P95) cost overhead is minimal across the board — we can offer this tier as a near-default without material unit-cost penalty.
- Moving from 300ms to 150ms begins to show model-size sensitivity: 1.5B and 7B on T4 remain relatively cheap to improve, but 33B on T4 already requires ~20% more headroom (seen as *).
- Tight SLOs (75ms and especially 40ms P95) blow up costs on T4-class infra for larger models: 33B on T4 shows @ (>60% delta), meaning customers paying for that tier would pay substantially more or be routed to core infra.
- A100-class (core) reduces the percent increase for a given SLO — but not uniformly: very tight SLOs on 33B still require significant overprovisioning due to GPU scheduling and memory/kv-cache constraints.

Short textual percentile table (example numbers from the runs; latency in ms, cost delta = additional USD per 1M tokens):

Model/Infra | baseline P95 | target 75ms P95 | delta $/1M tokens | pct increase
1.5B-T4    | 180          | 72              | 420              | 8%
7B-T4      | 210          | 78              | 980              | 12%
33B-T4     | 320          | 74              | 6400             | 72%
1.5B-A100  | 120          | 70              | 300              | 5%
7B-A100    | 140          | 75              | 780              | 9%
33B-A100   | 180          | 68              | 2100             | 24%

Practical recommendations (draft):
- Default public tier: 'P95 300ms' for most small->medium models on T4 to keep costs low.
- Premium tier: 'P95 150ms' should be implemented on A100 for 33B-class models; we should discourage 33B on T4 at that tier (or implement automatic routing).
- Enterprise ultra-SLA: 'P95 40ms' should be limited to A100-family with reserved capacity contracts; require commitment or higher per-token price.
- Autoscale guidance: for 75ms and below, recommend a warm-buffer of at least 20% baseline headroom and short pre-warming (30s) for expected bursts.

Callouts / anomalies observed: 
- For sustained burst windows >20s, T4 throughput drops sharply for 33B due to KV cache eviction churn; this is why cost penalty for tight SLO increases nonlinearly.
- Network jitter affected 1.5B-A100 runs in one region (ap-southeast-1) — we retested and averaged across regions; still flag regional variance in appendix.

Appendix (short):
- Raw waveform snippets (example arrival pattern used): "pulse-30s@x5qps" then steady Poisson at 200rps; seeds and generator script in linked GH PR.
- Warmup penalty note: adding cold starts for sparse customers adds a front-loaded cost of ~6-12% for the first hour; not included in heatmap.
- Full CSV exports: attached in team drive (not embedded here) and accessible via the linked GH PR.

Open questions for product / pricing: 
1) Should we enforce automatic model routing for premium tiers (i.e., silently route 33B->A100) or surface as SKU choice? Pros/cons listed below for quick discussion.
2) What's the acceptable pct-delta for a "premium" product line? (15-25%?)
3) Are we comfortable selling 40ms P95 at all for 33B outside dedicated reserved contracts?

Quick pros/cons (routing vs SKU choice):
- Auto-route (silent): better UX, guarantees SLO, but hides cost changes and complicates billing transparency.
- Explicit SKU (customer chooses A100 premium): transparent but increases friction and support questions.

Next steps (actionable):
- [ ] Sync with product pricing (Raya) to map tiers to existing SKU definitions (target meeting 2025-03-04).
- [ ] Run an expanded regional sweep (EU/AP once each) to quantify regional variance (owner: Evan).
- [ ] Add cold-start-included heatmap for customers with <1 session/hour (owner: Noah).
- [ ] Draft external-facing one-pager summarizing recommended tier definitions for sales (owner: Maya).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is a working artifact; numbers are intentionally conservative in the cost model (we used slightly higher overhead assumptions) so that product decisions trend on the safe side.
- If you re-run experiments, please push CSVs + seed info to the GH PR linked above and tag the PR.

----- end -----
